workflows.name: KYC Onboarding Lifecycle
workflows.trigger: A new party submits identity documents to start using the platform.
steps: Submit identity documents
Run identity verification
Screen against sanctions/PEP lists
Compliance officer reviews if flagged
Approve or reject the case
Activate the party on approval

workflows.name: Payment Lifecycle
workflows.trigger: Customer or partner initiates a payment in or out of the platform.
steps: Initiate payment
Authorize/screen for fraud
Submit to payment rail
Settle or fail
Reverse if disputed

workflows.name: Loan Lifecycle
workflows.trigger: Customer applies for a loan.
steps: Submit application
Underwrite (credit check, affordability)
Approve or reject
Disburse funds
Collect scheduled repayments
Close on payoff or mark default

workflows.name: Dispute Lifecycle
workflows.trigger: Customer disputes a payment they don't recognize or weren't satisfied with.
steps: Customer opens dispute
Support agent investigates
Rule in favor of customer or merchant
Close case

workflows.name: Reconciliation Workflow
workflows.trigger: Scheduled or on-demand reconciliation run against an external statement/feed.
steps: Import external statement/feed
Auto-match against ledger entries
Flag discrepancies
Resolve or escalate

workflows.name: Card Issuance & Control Lifecycle
workflows.trigger: A party requests a virtual or physical card, or an administrator issues one at account opening.
steps: Customer or administrator requests a card
Card issuing processor creates and tokenizes the card (PAN)
Physical card is shipped and activated by the customer, or a virtual card is activated immediately
Customer sets spend limits, merchant-category restrictions, or freezes the card as needed
Card expires at term end or is cancelled by the customer/administrator

provenance.notes: Lifecycle stages reasoned from card-issuing-processor conventions (Marqeta/Galileo/Lithic-style APIs), corroborated by EMVCo's card-personalization specs and moov-io/iso8583's authorization message model; not directly modeled in either OSS ledger reviewed.

workflows.name: Wallet Funding & Withdrawal
workflows.trigger: Customer tops up a wallet from an external source or withdraws wallet balance to an external account.
steps: Customer initiates a top-up or withdrawal
Platform checks per-transaction, daily, and velocity limits
Request is routed to the payment rail (inbound top-up or outbound withdrawal)
Ledger posts the balancing double-entry once the rail confirms
Wallet balance reflects the updated total

provenance.notes: Reuses the payment state machine for the top-up/withdrawal leg; wallet-level funding pattern corroborated by Blnk's balance/transaction model and Fineract's savings-account deposit/withdrawal APIs.

workflows.name: Internal & P2P Transfer
workflows.trigger: Customer moves money between their own wallets/accounts, or sends money to another party by handle, phone number, or account identifier.
steps: Customer selects source and destination (own account, or another party's handle)
Platform resolves the recipient handle for P2P transfers
Platform validates transfer limits
Ledger posts the same-platform balancing entries
Both parties are notified of the completed transfer

workflows.name: Interest Accrual
workflows.trigger: Scheduled daily or monthly job runs against interest-bearing balances and outstanding loan principal.
steps: Identify interest-bearing accounts and loans due for accrual
Compute accrued interest for the period
Post accrual to the ledger
Capitalize accrued interest into principal/balance on the scheduled date

provenance.notes: Fineract's savings/loan accrual jobs are the primary evidence; no second OSS implementation reviewed for this specific workflow.

workflows.name: Statement Generation
workflows.trigger: Scheduled period-end job (typically monthly) generates statements for active accounts.
steps: Identify accounts due for a period-end statement
Aggregate ledger entries within the statement period
Compute opening and closing balances
Render and store the statement document
Notify the customer that a new statement is available

workflows.name: Fee Assessment
workflows.trigger: A chargeable event occurs: a payment, card transaction, or period close matches a fee schedule.
steps: Match the triggering event to a fee schedule
Compute the fee amount (flat, percentage, or tiered)
Assess the fee against the account
Post the fee as a ledger entry
Finance ops can waive an assessed fee on request

workflows.name: Fraud Alert Triage
workflows.trigger: The fraud/risk scoring engine flags a payment above its risk threshold.
steps: System scores the transaction in real time and opens a fraud alert
Risk analyst triages the alert queue
Analyst clears the alert, confirms fraud, or escalates to compliance for AML review
Confirmed fraud blocks the card/party and closes the alert

provenance.notes: Real-time scoring/triage pattern reasoned from industry-standard fraud architecture, corroborated by moov-io/iso8583's authorization/response-code model and PSD2 SCA's transaction-risk-analysis provisions; not directly modeled in either OSS ledger reviewed.

workflows.name: FX Conversion
workflows.trigger: A payment or transfer crosses currencies on a multi-currency ledger.
steps: Quote an FX rate for the conversion
Lock the rate for the transaction
Convert the amount
Post ledger entries in both source and destination currencies
Settle the converted amount

provenance.notes: Per-currency balance model corroborated by Blnk; currency-code terminology from ISO 4217. FX-rate-locking mechanics are reasoned, not directly observed in the source reviewed.

workflows.name: Mandate & Recurring Payment
workflows.trigger: Customer sets up a standing order, subscription-style recurring payment, or a one-off bill payment to a registered biller.
steps: Customer defines the payee/biller and recurrence rule (or a one-off amount for bill pay)
Platform validates the mandate against available funds and limits
Payment executes automatically on each due date (or immediately for bill pay)
Failed executions are retried with backoff
Customer can cancel the standing mandate at any time

provenance.notes: ISO 20022 standing-order message types and moov-io/ach's NACHA-standard ACH file support corroborate the payment-rail mechanics; the recurrence/mandate scheduling itself is reasoned, not directly modeled in either source.

workflows.name: Savings Goal
workflows.trigger: Customer creates a savings goal (a labeled sub-balance, or 'pot') with a target amount.
steps: Customer creates a goal with a target amount and optional deadline
Customer funds the goal via manual transfer or an automatic round-up rule
Platform tracks progress toward the target
Customer withdraws from or marks the goal complete

provenance.notes: Neobank 'pot'/goal framing corroborated by Actual Budget's category goal-template feature (MIT-licensed, inspected via API, not cloned); Fineract's savings-product model supports the underlying labeled-balance pattern.

workflows.name: Spend Insights Generation
workflows.trigger: Scheduled job runs after new transactions post, to categorize and summarize spend.
steps: Fetch newly posted payments
Match each payment to a merchant category (MCC)
Categorize the transaction
Aggregate spend trends for the period
Surface insights to the customer

provenance.notes: Merchant categorization corroborated by ISO 18245 MCC codes and Actual Budget's category-based spending reports (MIT-licensed, inspected via API, not cloned).

workflows.name: Virtual Account Provisioning
workflows.trigger: A party needs a dedicated incoming-funds identifier separate from their primary account number.
steps: Administrator or system requests a virtual account number for the party
Platform allocates a number from its account-numbering pool
Number is linked to the party's underlying ledger account
Incoming funds referencing the virtual number are auto-allocated to that account

workflows.name: Open Banking Consent
workflows.trigger: A third-party provider requests access to account information or payment initiation under PSD2.
steps: Customer is redirected to authenticate with the platform
Customer grants a scoped consent (account information and/or payment initiation)
Third-party provider calls the AISP or PISP API within the granted scope
Customer can view and revoke active consents at any time

provenance.notes: Directly defined by PSD2 and its SCA RTS (AISP/PISP consent-and-access model).

workflows.name: Webhook Delivery
workflows.trigger: A subscribed lifecycle event occurs (payment, account, or card state change).
steps: Build the event payload
Sign the payload
Attempt delivery to the partner's registered endpoint
Retry with exponential backoff on failure
Mark the event delivered or move it to a dead-letter queue after max retries

workflows.name: Account Closure
workflows.trigger: Customer or administrator requests to close a ledger account.
steps: Verify the account balance is zero (or transfer/withdraw the remainder)
Settle any pending transactions
Revoke or cancel cards linked to the account
Close the account
Retain records for the regulatory retention period
